crime_highlights: Mr. Parranto entered guilty pleas on two counts of possession of fentanyl for the purposes of trafficking in a wholesale commercial operation
two counts of illegal possession of a loaded handgun for use in the trafficking operation
Mr. Parranto was under a lifetime firearm prohibition
police recovered 485.12 g of fentanyl powder (capable of producing 500,000 individual doses)
rationale_highlights: It was incumbent on the sentencing judge and the Court of Appeal to consider these circumstances
Mr. Parranto’s background circumstances can be said to have played a part in bringing him before the court
Based on the gravity of the offence, Gladue factors and the aggravating and mitigating circumstances, we agree with the Court of Appeal that a global sentence of 14 years is appropriate
note: Gladue weighed but sentence increased; no explicit culpability reduction.

crime_highlights: her suitcase was found to contain 1.97 kilograms of cocaine
her partner had promised to pay her $20,000 to bring the suitcase to Canada
the prospect of homelessness for her child motivated her to agree to her partner’s request
rationale_highlights: This report revealed a life of significant hardship and intergenerational trauma

We accept entirely that the circumstances which led Ms. Sharma to import drugs are tragic and that her moral culpability was thereby attenuated (which was reflected in a sentence of 18 months rather than the 6 years initially proposed by the Crown)
note: Crime passage has no victim harm; drug importation.

crime_highlights: Mr. Hilbach and a 13-year-old accomplice robbed a convenience store in Edmonton with an unloaded sawed-off rifle
Mr. Hilbach pointed the rifle at two employees and demanded cash
his accomplice punched one employee and kicked the other
rationale_highlights: which established that his family had a history of residential school attendance, struggled with addictions to alcohol or other substances, and suffered financial difficulties
His personal history is marked by physical abuse, family violence, chronic unemployment, and gang involvement
Though Mr. Hilbach’s personal circumstances attenuate his culpability somewhat
note: Culpability attenuated only somewhat; five-year minimum upheld.
